config.title: Watching Films in English in Berlin: FAQ
config.subtitle: The abbreviations, the cinemas and how to find an English screening tonight.

items.q: What does OmU mean on a Berlin cinema listing?
items.a: **OmU stands for Original mit Untertiteln**, the original soundtrack with **German** subtitles. If the film is in English you will hear the English and can simply ignore the German text at the bottom. If the film is in another language, the only subtitles are German, so look for an **OmeU** screening (English subtitles) instead.

items.q: What is the difference between OV, OmU and OmeU?
items.a: **OV or OF** (Originalversion or Originalfassung) is the original language with no subtitles at all. **OmU** is the original audio with German subtitles. **OmeU** (sometimes OmenglU) is the original audio with English subtitles. All three keep the original voices, unlike a dubbed version.

items.q: Where can I watch films in English in Berlin?
items.a: Reliable options in the centre are **Kino International** on Karl-Marx-Allee, **Babylon Mitte** at Rosa-Luxemburg-Platz, and **Hackesche Höfe Kino** in the courtyards near where my walking tour ends. In the west, the **Delphi** cinemas and the **Zoo Palast** show many films in the original. The **Yorck group** lists all its original-version screenings in one place.

items.q: How do I find an English screening tonight?
items.a: Two local sites collect only the original-version showings across Berlin: **ovkino.de** and **ov-berlin.de**. Both let you filter by cinema and by language, so you can pick a screening near where you already are. The Yorck group's own site also has an original-version filter.

items.q: Are films in Berlin dubbed or subtitled by default?
items.a: Most cinemas show the **German-dubbed version** by default, marked **DF** (Deutsche Fassung) or **synchronisiert**. A listing with no language label at all is almost always dubbed too. The original versions are the ones marked OV, OmU or OmeU, so look for those letters.

items.q: Is Kino International open again after the renovation?
items.a: Yes. **Kino International reopened in early 2026** after an eighteen-month heritage restoration, with its silver premiere curtain rebuilt and a new laser projector fitted. It is back to screening original-version films and premieres, and the 1960s hall alone is worth the ticket.

items.q: How much is a cinema ticket in Berlin, and can I pay by card?
items.a: In 2026 a ticket usually costs around 9 to 14 euros, and **Monday and Tuesday are cheaper nights** at many cinemas. The big multiplexes take cards, but a few small independents still prefer cash, so carry a little. Remember that the adverts run first, so the feature starts ten to fifteen minutes after the time on your ticket. Checked on 20 August 2026.
